questions.question: The reaction of an acid and a metal gives :

options.text: carbon dioxide, salt and hydrogen gas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**hydrogen gas and salt**__

__
 
• The reaction between an acid and a metal produces **hydrogen gas and salt**.
 
• This type of reaction is a common example of a single displacement reaction where the metal displaces hydrogen from the acid.
 
• The general equation for this reaction is:

 **Metal + Acid → Salt + Hydrogen gas**.
 
• For example, when zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid, zinc chloride and hydrogen gas are produced:

 **Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Not all metals react with acids to produce hydrogen gas. For example, copper does not react with dilute hydrochloric acid.
 
• The reactivity of a metal with an acid depends on its position in the reactivity series. Metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series will typically displace hydrogen from acids.
 
• Safety note: Hydrogen gas is flammable, and care should be taken to avoid ignition sources when performing such reactions.

questions.question: What type of mirror is used for beard making?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concave**__.

__Concept:__

__
 
• Mirrors are surfaces that reflect light creating images of objects in front of them.
 
• Mirrors are of two types-

 
• Plane mirrors
 
• Spherical mirrors (Concave and Convex mirrors)

 
• **Plane mirrors - **

 
 
• The image formed by the plane mirror is virtual and erect i.e. image cannot be projected or focused on a screen.

 Plane mirrors are the most widely used mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Spherical mirrors (Concave and Convex mirrors)**
 
• Concave mirrors
 
 
• A spherical mirror, whose reflecting surface is curved inwards, that is, faces towards the center of the sphere, is called a concave mirror.​
 
 
 
• Convex mirrors
 
 
• A spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is curved outwards, is called a convex mirror.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/de27fee40b9ba7ee1bbd9bc37707d7367c60ea09565bbd975e38e4fd5814de11.png] 

**Explanation:**__

__
 
• A **concave mirror is used for beard making mirrors**__ because when the **concave mirror is placed very close to the object, a magnified and virtual image is obtained.**
 
• Concave mirrors are curved inward, and they have reflective surfaces that curve toward the viewer.
 
• Concave mirror produces a virtual, erect and magnified image of our face when held in front of the face at a distance less than its focal length thus, allowing us to closely observe our face.
 
• The **magnification effect of a concave mirror allows users to focus on specific areas, such as trimming a beard** or applying makeup, with more precision.

Thus, __**Concave mirror is used for beard making.**__

questions.question: When sodium sulphate solution is added to barium chloride solution, precipitate of _______ is formed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**barium sulphate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When sodium sulphate (Na₂SO₄) solution is added to barium chloride (BaCl₂) solution, a chemical reaction occurs.
 
• The reaction leads to the formation of a white precipitate of barium sulphate (BaSO₄).
 
• The balanced chemical equation for this reaction is: Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → 2NaCl + BaSO₄.
 
• Barium sulphate is insoluble in water, which is why it forms a precipitate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Precipitation Reaction**

 
 
• A precipitation reaction occurs when two soluble salts react in aqueous solution to form one or more insoluble products.
 
• The insoluble product formed is known as the precipitate.
 
 
 
• **Solubility Rules**
 
 
• Solubility rules help predict whether a precipitate will form in a chemical reaction.
 
• According to these rules, sulphates are generally soluble, but barium sulphate is an exception and is insoluble.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Barium Sulphate**
 
 
• Barium sulphate is used in medical imaging as a radiocontrast agent for X-ray imaging and other diagnostic procedures.
 
• It is also used in the production of pigments, paper coatings, and as a filler in plastics and rubber.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Safety**
 
 
• Barium compounds can be toxic, but barium sulphate is considered safe due to its insolubility in water and the human body.
 
• Handling of barium chloride and sodium sulphate should be done with appropriate safety measures, including gloves and eye protection.

questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at a certain rate of simple interest. In how many years will it become four times of itself at the same rate of simple interest ?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Time taken for a sum of money to double itself: 8 years Rate of simple interest: Constant

**Concept used: **

The formula for simple interest is:

Simple Interest = Principal × Rate × Time

**Calculation: **

Let's denote the initial principal as "P" and the rate of interest as "r".

According to the given information, the sum of money doubles itself in 8 years.

This means the simple interest earned is equal to the principal:

Simple Interest = Principal = P

Using the formula for simple interest, we have: P = P × r × 8

Simplifying the equation: r = 1 / 8

To find the time it takes for the sum of money to become four times itself, we need to solve for time. Let's denote the time as "t".

According to the formula for simple interest, when the sum of money becomes four times itself, the simple interest earned is three times the principal:

⇒ Simple Interest = Principal × Rate × ​Time 3P = P × (1/8) × t

Simplifying the equation: 3 = 1/8 × t

⇒ t = 24

**Therefore, the sum of money will become four times itself at the same rate of simple interest in 24 years. **

questions.question: The term _______ refers to the densely packed kidney filtration unit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Glomerulus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The glomerulus is a network of capillaries located at the beginning of a nephron in the kidney.
 
• It is involved in the filtration of blood to form urine.
 
• The glomerulus allows the passage of water, ions, and small molecules from the blood into the Bowman's capsule.
 
• It retains large molecules like proteins and blood cells within the bloodstream.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nephron**

 
 
• The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney responsible for urine formation.
 
• Each nephron includes a glomerulus and a renal tubule.
 
• There are approximately 1 million nephrons in each human kidney.
 
• The nephron performs essential functions like filtration, reabsorption, secretion, and excretion.
 
 
 
• **Bowman's Capsule**
 
 
• The Bowman's capsule is a cup-like sac that encases the glomerulus.
 
• It collects the filtrate that emerges from the glomerulus.
 
• This structure initiates the process of filtering blood to form urine.
 
 
 
• **Renal Tubule**
 
 
• The renal tubule processes the filtrate from the Bowman's capsule.
 
• It includes segments like the proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle, distal convoluted tubule, and collecting duct.
 
• Each segment plays a specific role in reabsorbing water and solutes or secreting substances into the filtrate.
 
 
 
• **Filtration Barrier**
 
 
• The filtration barrier in the glomerulus consists of three layers: endothelial cells, basement membrane, and podocytes.
 
• It selectively allows the passage of small molecules while preventing large molecules like proteins from passing through.
 
• This barrier is crucial for maintaining the composition of blood and filtrate.

__
 
• **Gravity **is the phrase used to describe the **attraction force** that the **earth exerts **on any object. Gravity is a force that all **objects** are **drawn to**.
 
• **Satellites **can **orbit **a body and fall around it rather than into it if the speed and** gravity** are just right.
 
• The **centripetal force** required to keep planets in orbit around the Sun and all kinds of satellites in orbit** around** the **Earth** is provided by **gravitational attraction.**
 
• The **Moon** continues to** orbit** the **Earth** because of **gravity**. The velocity of the Moon is continuously shifting in one direction.
 
• *Therefore, the force of attraction of the earth provides the centripetal force for the motion of the moon around the earth.​​*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A "**centripetal**" force is the name given to the **ongoing pull** on the Moon as it revolves around the Earth. The "**centrifugal" force**, which pulls on the Earth and keeps the moon in motion,** balances** this force.
 
• Any force that induces a **shift in velocity** direction toward the** center** of a **circular motion** is referred to as a** centripetal force.** Centripetal force is caused by the part of the force that is **perpendicular** to the velocity.
 
• This force causes a body to travel along a** curved route**. It always moves in the opposite direction of the body's motion and in the direction of the **immediate center** of the path's curvature.
